column1: # links.tsv -- every path this repo deploys, and where it goes.
# install.sh links individual FILES, never whole directories, so Hyprland and
# Noctalia can still create their own files alongside yours without fighting
# the repo. A `tree` row means "every file under here", walked and linked one
# by one; it does not mean the directory itself is linked.
# Symlinks are safe for everything here:
#   ~/.config/hypr/*      Hyprland only ever reads its config.
#   ~/.config/noctalia/*  Noctalia only ever reads ~/.config/noctalia. It saves
#                         GUI changes to ~/.local/state/noctalia/settings.toml,
#                         a different tree -- so the app can never clobber a
#                         tracked file or replace a link.
#   ~/.config/yazi/*      read-only as far as yazi is concerned.
#   ~/.local/bin/noct-*   plain scripts.
# Format: section <TAB> kind <TAB> source <TAB> root <TAB> destination
#   section  the heading it is reported under, and the order rows run in
#   kind     file       link this one file
#            tree       link every file under this directory, recursively
#            exec-tree  the same, and chmod +x the source first
#   source   relative to the repository root
#   root     config  ->  $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (~/.config)
#            bin     ->  ~/.local/bin
#   destination  relative to that root; "." means straight into it
# Two kinds of file are skipped inside a tree, by rule rather than by row:
# README.md, because documentation belongs in the repo rather than scattered
# through ~/.config, and *.example, because those are meant to be COPIED to a
# new name (host.lua, glass.local.conf) and edited -- a symlink into the repo
# cannot be either.

# Shown in every new shell by /usr/share/cachyos-fish-config, which
# config/fish/config.fish sources. fastfetch only reads it. Its options get
# renamed between releases (logo.recache became logo.cache in 2.70), and
# fastfetch reports a stale one as an error in every new shell.
configs
# The colourscheme, from the submodule at vendor/noirblaze. It used to be a
# tracked file at config/noctalia/palettes/noirblaze.json, and it is not any
# more: the same theme drives neovim, and keeping two hand-edited copies in step
# is exactly the drift this repo's whole shape is against.
# Note the source is OUTSIDE config/. install/lib/link.sh links "$REPO/$src", so
# any path in the checkout works; nothing in the engine needed changing.
# The row has to be a `file` rather than letting the `tree` row above pick it up,
# because the tree row walks config/noctalia and the palette no longer lives
# there. Both rows claiming ~/.config/noctalia/palettes/noirblaze.json is what
# `tests/lint.sh manifest-collisions` exists to catch, and deleting the tracked
# file is what stops it.
configs
# aerc.conf only. accounts.conf is NOT tracked -- it names mail addresses,
# server names and a credential command -- so config/aerc/ ships an .example
# to copy, which the linker skips by the same rule that skips
# glass.local.conf.example.
configs
# Read by uwsm before the compositor starts, and the only place the session
# gets ~/.local/bin on PATH -- which is what the launcher providers and the
# noct-glass binds are found through. See config/uwsm/env.
configs
# The same PATH, through the systemd user manager instead, for the case where
# the session was started without uwsm. See config/environment.d.
configs
# User units: noctalia.service, which autostart.lua starts so that a crashed
# shell comes back by itself, and the helpers lib/lid.lua and lib/rotate.lua
# start and stop. Linked per file like everything else, so
# `systemctl --user enable` can still drop its own .wants links beside them.
configs
# Launcher flags for the Chromium family. Each launcher reads its own file
# straight out of ~/.config -- brave-flags.conf, chromium-flags.conf,
# signal-desktop-flags.conf -- so these are `file` rows into the root, not a
# tree. They live beside the rest of each app's config; the policy files next
# to them go through browsers.tsv instead, because those need root.
configs
